page_title: 6 Rules of thumb to build blazing fast web server applications

sources.entry: 6 Rules of thumb to build blazing fast web server applications

summary.title: 6 Rules of thumb to build blazing fast web server applications
summary.one_liner: Six backend performance principles for web apps (avoid premature optimization, do less work, defer tasks, cache, avoid N+1 queries, scale horizontally), with PHP-focused tools and examples.
takeaways: Profile first with tools like xdebug, xhprof, or Blackfire before optimizing, and avoid premature optimization.
Do only the work a request needs: use autoloading, dependency injection, and lazy loading.
Defer slow tasks such as sending email or resizing images to job queues processed by workers.
Use caching at several levels (bytecode, application, HTTP, reverse proxy) and plan for invalidation; avoid N+1 queries with eager loading or joins.
Prepare for horizontal scaling by moving sessions and user files out of local disk into shared storage.
summary.summary: The article lists six rules for backend web application performance, each illustrated mostly with PHP examples but presented as applicable to any language. It covers profiling before optimizing, reducing unnecessary work through autoloading, dependency injection and lazy loading, and deferring heavy tasks to job queues. It then explains caching layers (bytecode, application, HTTP, reverse proxy), the N+1 query problem, and horizontal scaling concerns around sessions and file storage. Each section links to tools and further reading.
